Certainly! Here’s an example of a chat message exchange where one user is attempting to spam the other with unsolicited messages, likely for promotional or malicious purposes:

---

**User A (Spammer):**
*"Hey! Check out this amazing deal! 🚀 Only $9.99 for lifetime access to our premium service! Click here: [suspicious-link.com] Don’t miss out!!!"*

**User B (Recipient):**
*"I’m not interested. Please stop messaging me."*

**User A (Spammer):**
*"But wait! There’s more! 🎁 Limited-time offer! Sign up now and get a FREE bonus! [another-suspicious-link.com] Act fast before it’s gone!"*

**User B (Recipient):**
*"I said no. Stop spamming me or I’ll report you."*

**User A (Spammer):**
*"You’re missing out! 😢 Last chance! [same-suspicious-link.com] Trust me, you won’t regret it!"*

---

In this example, **User A** is clearly ignoring **User B’s** requests to stop, repeatedly sending unsolicited promotional links, which is a common spamming tactic. **User B** is rightfully setting boundaries and threatening to report the behavior, which is the appropriate response to spam.

If you encounter spam like this, most platforms allow you to **block, mute, or report** the user to prevent further harassment.
